# Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā (Atk Abh03a)

**ID:** Atk Abh03a  
**Section:** Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā (atk-abh03)  
**Collection:** Atthakatha-Abhidhamma

**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/](https://tipitaka.org/romn/)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* (also known under the collective commentary title *Paramatthadīpanī*) is the Theravāda Abhidhamma commentary covering the final five treatises of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Collins 1998; Nyanatusita 2008]. In traditional bibliographies, its individual components are classified sequentially as *Pañca-pakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* I through V, comprising commentaries on the *Dhātukathā* (Part I), *Puggalapaññatti* (Part II), *Kathāvatthu* (Part III), *Yamaka* (Part IV), and *Paṭṭhāna* (including the *Tikapaṭṭhāna*) [Collins 1998; Nyanatusita 2008]. In the Pali scholastic tradition, the work is attributed to the fifth-century commentator Buddhaghosa [Nyanatusita 2008]. Later subcommentarial literature composed on these texts includes the *Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* (also called *Paramatthapakāsanī*) and the *Pañcapakaraṇa-anuṭīkā* [Nyanatusita 2008].

**Sources**

- [Collins 1998] Steven Collins, Nirvana and other Buddhist Felicities: Utopias of the Pali imaginaire (Cambridge University Press, 1998) — Lists the commentary and associates it with Tikapaṭṭhāna
- [Nyanatusita 2008] Bhikkhu Nyanatusita, Reference Table of Pali Literature (2008) — Documents divisions I–IV (Dhātukathā-, Puggalapaññatti-, Kathāvatthu-, Yamaka-aṭṭhakathā), the alternative title Paramatthadīpanī, and attribution to Buddhaghosa
